subject: Bareword CALL in a package-switched region resolves to the enclosing package's sub instead of dying
description: Pre-existing (probed s379 on both 5d94161 and c99ca41, identical): `sub hello { print "main hello\n" } sub t { package P; hello(); } t();` — perl dies "Undefined subroutine &P::hello called"; PCL calls main::hello and prints. The s378 review-request claim "bareword CALLS inside such a region are ALREADY homed to X correctly" holds only for the direction where the sub EXISTS in X; when it does not, PCL falls back to the enclosing/main sub — a silent wrong-callee, not just error-text divergence. Suspect the runtime's sub-resolution fallback chain (or the lowering resolving the callee at read time in the section package). Discriminating measurement to carry: transpile the probe and read whether the emitted call is `(pl-hello)` interned in the SECTION package (reader problem, sibling of #239's variable half) or a runtime name lookup with a main fallback (runtime problem). Fix at whichever layer diverges; probe the exists-in-P direction as the inverse guard. Filed from the s379 Fable review (probe p4c in docs/fable-answers-s378.md).
